sections.html:
Hamblen County is small, at 176 square miles, and daily life centers on Morristown, the seat and largest city. Other named places include White Pine, Russellville, Whitesburg, Talbott, Lowland and Witt. Interstate 81, US 11E and US 25E cross the county.

About 68,843 residents lived here in July 2025, 6.7 percent more than in 2020. There are 28,945 housing units, and owners occupy 69.8 percent of them, which leaves a larger share of rentals than many nearby counties. The median home value is $210,900 and household income is $55,454. Builders pulled 258 permits in 2025.

sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Hamblen County
sections.html:
One building covers the main offices: the Hamblen County Courthouse at 511 West Second North Street, Morristown, TN 37814. Reach the Assessor of Property at 423-586-1852. That office values about 32,000 parcels worth more than $3 billion in appraised value and prepares the roll used by the county and by the City of Morristown.

The Trustee collects the money, at 423-586-6290. The trustee is also the county's treasurer and banker, so every dollar the county receives passes through that office. A satellite counter at 2415 N Davy Crockett Parkway also takes tax payments.

Fourteen commissioners set the rate and meet the Thursday after each third Monday at 5:30 p.m. Ask the trustee for the final county rate and whether Morristown adds its own tax to your address.

sections.h2: How the tax bill is worked out
sections.html:
The assessor appraises, state law applies a ratio, and the rate does the rest. Assessed value is 25 percent of appraised value for houses and farms, 40 percent for commercial and industrial property.

For a rough bill, start from the appraised value, apply the ratio, divide by 100, then multiply by the rate. The trustee can confirm the real rate.

The assessor's office also runs reappraisal. After a countywide reappraisal, a jump in value is not proof of an error, and a judge may disregard it. The owner must still bring evidence of the right value.

Check the notice you receive each year for the appraised value, and compare it with what similar houses nearby have sold for. If your number looks high, that comparison is the start of an appeal. Ask the trustee whether the city sends a separate bill for your address.

sections.h2: Due dates and where to pay
sections.html:
Hamblen's tax page lists October 1 as the due date and March 1 of the following year as delinquency. The state calendar sets the start of payment at the first Monday in October.

Hamblen County property tax calendar
DateWhat happens
January 1Ownership and condition set for the year
June 1Equalization board begins its session
First Monday of OctoberPayments open
End of FebruaryLast interest-free day
March 1Delinquent

You can pay in three places:

  • At the trustee's counter in the courthouse on West Second North Street
  • At the satellite office on N Davy Crockett Parkway
  • Online through TNPayments.com/Hamblen, a link that leaves the county site

Questions go to 423-586-6290. Businesses pay tax on equipment to the same office on the same calendar. The gross receipts tax goes to the County Clerk at 423-586-1993.

Phone the assessor first. The office is also the contact for the local equalization board, whose five members the county commission appoints and which sits once a year, beginning June 1. An informal talk with an assessor can help but never counts as an appeal, so ask whether Hamblen offers one and still file with the board.

Unhappy with the board? Next is the State Board of Equalization, where the filing deadline is August 1 or, if later, forty-five days after notice. An administrative judge takes the case and rules within 90 days. The person appealing must prove the value. Scheduling goes through 615-401-7883, extension 2.

Proof that tends to work:

  • Sold houses comparable to yours, adjusted for their differences
  • An appraisal, with the appraiser available to testify
  • A specific figure you propose, supported by facts about the house

You must also pay the part of the bill you do not dispute, and any older unpaid years, by the delinquency date.

Hamblen has both. Under the state relief program, low-income seniors, disabled owners and some disabled military service members get part of the tax refunded. The 2026 ceiling is $38,470 of 2025 income. Refunds for seniors and disabled owners cover up to $33,600 of value, and the figure for disabled military service members is $175,000. Applications go to the trustee, who must receive them within 35 days of the delinquency date.

Hamblen is also on the state's list of 28 counties with a freeze. It joined in 2007, and the 2026 income limit is $39,260. A homeowner who reaches 65 by year end and passes the income test can lock the tax on a main residence at the first qualifying year's amount. Each year requires a new application, and the fixed amount grows if the owner improves the property or moves to a different house.

Ownership is measured on January 1, yet the title company divides the year's bill between buyer and seller at closing. Ask the trustee for your balance before you list. That matters most for an inherited house or one with several unpaid years, since interest starts once March 1 goes by.

The Clerk and Master, at 423-586-9112, keeps a delinquent tax section on its website, along with a tax search and payment tool. After closing, take the deed to the Register of Deeds, also in the courthouse, where the state recording taxes are paid.

A short plan helps. Call the trustee at 423-586-6290 and ask for the balance on every year, not just the current one. Call the assessor at 423-586-1852 and confirm the name and parcel details on your record. If you plan to dispute the value, remember that the local board opens June 1 and that you still owe the undisputed part of the bill. If the house is vacant or inherited, note that the delinquency clock runs from March 1 whether or not anyone lives there. A cash buyer can often close quickly enough to pay arrears from proceeds before the bill grows.

For a lender-financed buyer, the title company will want a clear balance. For a cash sale, the same balance still gets cleared from your proceeds at closing. Either way, keep your last bill and your deed handy when you call, since staff may ask for the parcel or owner name.

faqs.q: When are Hamblen County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The county's tax page gives October 1. Bills turn delinquent the following March 1. Payment is taken at the courthouse counter, at the Davy Crockett Parkway satellite office, or through TNPayments.com/Hamblen.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Hamblen County property assessment?
faqs.a: The assessor's office, 511 West Second North Street, Morristown. The number is 423-586-1852. The office values roughly 32,000 parcels.

faqs.q: Does Hamblen County have a property tax freeze?
faqs.a: Yes, adopted in 2007, with a 2026 income limit of $39,260. Applicants must be 65 by the end of the year, own and live in the home, and reapply with the trustee each year.

faqs.q: How do I dispute my Hamblen County property value?
faqs.a: Call the assessor, then go before the local equalization board, which opens June 1. After that, the state board takes an appeal filed by August 1 or within forty-five days of the local notice, whichever comes later.

faqs.q: Where can I pay Hamblen County property tax online?
faqs.a: Use TNPayments.com/Hamblen, the link on the county's tax page. For balance questions, call the trustee at 423-586-6290.
